sections.h2: Who records a deed in Columbiana County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The Columbiana County Recorder records deeds for every parcel in the county, from Salem and East Liverpool to the smallest townships. The office is tied to the historic courthouse in Lisbon, the county seat, and its phone number is 330-424-9517. Under ORC 5301.25, a deed is recorded in the county where the land lies, and until that happens the statute treats it as fraudulent against a later buyer who had no knowledge of it. A sale is not finished at the closing table. It is finished when the deed is filed in Lisbon.

The recorder's own website says the office keeps deeds, mortgages, easements, military discharge paperwork and other documents that matter to commerce. Everything the office receives is recorded right away and can be searched, and the originals go back to the person who submitted them once quality control checks are done. The site also links to a property check notification form, which is worth a look for anyone who owns a house they do not live in.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Columbiana County?
sections.html:
The base price is set by state law, and the county adds only a small surcharge. The recorder's Documents & Fees page says the charge has two halves, a basic recording fee and an equal housing trust fund fee, with a preservation surcharge of no more than $5 per document that differs from county to county. Ask the office for the Columbiana County surcharge before you write the check, because that single figure is the one the state schedule leaves open.

The rates below are the ones printed in ORC 317.32 and the two auditor-side sections that follow it. Pages are 8.5 by 14 inches or a fraction of a page, and the caption page counts.

ChargeRate as printed in the Revised Code
Recording a deed, first two pages$17 base fee plus $17 housing trust fund fee
Each page after the second$4 base fee plus $4 housing trust fund fee
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5 per instrument, set by the county
Auditor conveyance fee (ORC 319.54)$1, or 10 cents per $100 or fraction of value, whichever is greater
Auditor transfer or entry fee (ORC 319.54)50 cents for each transfer or entry
Optional county transfer tax (ORC 322.02)Up to 30 cents per $100 or fraction of value, if the commissioners levy it

Ask the Columbiana County Auditor whether the county levies the optional transfer tax and at what rate. Do not assume the top rate applies.

sections.h2: What does the county auditor do before a Columbiana County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The auditor handles the value statement and the conveyance fee first, and the deed reaches the recorder with the auditor's endorsement on it. Under ORC 319.202, the buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement declaring the value of the property, and the seller pays the conveyance fee plus any county transfer tax. Value means the full price paid or to be paid, including the amount of any mortgage or vendor's lien on the property.

The statement carries two questions that matter in a farming county like this one. The seller is asked whether the house gets a homestead or owner-occupancy tax reduction, and whether the land was in the current agricultural use valuation program. If it was and it will not stay there, a recoupment charge can follow under ORC 5713.34, so the buyer and seller should settle who carries it before the paperwork goes in.

Some transfers pay no conveyance fee, but the exemption has to be stated on the form. The list in ORC 319.54 includes:

  • A gift between spouses, or between a parent and child or the spouse of either
  • A transfer among heirs or devisees of one decedent when no money is paid
  • A deed that only confirms or corrects an earlier recorded deed
  • A transfer to the grantor of a revocable trust, or from the grantor to the trustee
  • A transfer made under a court order, to the extent it is not a sale completed under that order

sections.h2: What has to be on the deed before it goes to Lisbon?
sections.html:
A deed has to be signed by the grantor, and the signature has to be acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor. That rule comes from ORC 5301.01. Most sellers use a notary at the title company, a bank or the lawyer who drafted the deed.

Before the auditor moves the property into the buyer's name, ORC 319.20 asks for a few items. Check each one before you leave the closing:

  • The last known address of the buyer, or of one of the buyers if there are several
  • A reference to the volume and page, or other identifier, of the deed by which the seller took title
  • The complete legal description that matches the tax list
  • The signed value statement and the conveyance payment described above

If only part of a parcel is being sold, the auditor splits the tax value between the piece sold and the piece kept. Any unpaid tax on the whole parcel is then divided in proportion to value when the buyer or remaining owner asks for it.

sections.h2: What is the county around Lisbon like for a seller?
sections.html:
Columbiana County sits on the eastern edge of Ohio, with Pennsylvania on its east side, Mahoning County to the north and about 20 miles of the Ohio River along the south. The county government's history page gives the area as 534 square miles in 18 townships. Its glacial boundary runs east to west and touches Lisbon, so the north is fertile farmland while the southern townships are hilly and rugged.

Lisbon was platted in 1803 by a Baptist minister and first called New Lisbon, and the county dropped the word New in 1895. Wikipedia's county article lists Salem as the largest city at 11,915 people in the 2020 census, ahead of East Liverpool at 9,958 and Columbiana at 6,559. Lisbon itself counted 2,597, and East Palestine, the site of the February 3, 2023 freight train derailment, counted 4,761. East Liverpool grew around a pottery industry that the county history calls distinctive, and brick, clay and foundry work followed in other towns.

sections.h2: How do Columbiana County housing numbers compare with the rest of Ohio?
sections.html:
Most homes in the county are owned rather than rented. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for Columbiana County shows these figures:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 99,377, down 2.5% from the April 2020 base of 101,900
  • Housing units: 46,220, with 41,459 households in 2020 to 2024
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 72.7%
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $151,600
  • Median gross rent: $756 a month
  • Median household income: $58,180, and 14.7% of residents in poverty
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 58

The permit count and the 2020 to 2024 median value are the two figures that describe how much new housing the county adds and what an existing house is worth to an owner-occupant. A county appraisal or a written cash offer will say more about one particular house.

sections.h2: What should a seller settle before the deed is filed?
sections.html:
A short checklist before the closing helps keep the filing from being sent back:

  • Ask the Columbiana County Treasurer for the current tax balance on the parcel so the title company can pay it from the proceeds
  • Ask any lender with a mortgage on the house to file a release, and confirm it reaches the recorder
  • If the owner died, ask the probate court which papers authorize a sale and who signs the deed
  • Compare the legal description on your last deed with the tax record before anyone drafts the new one
  • Decide who will carry any farm-use recoupment charge or unpaid assessment

When a house is sold as-is for cash, these same steps apply. The deed, the value statement and the recording still run through the auditor and the recorder in Lisbon in the same order.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Columbiana County?
faqs.a: Record it with the Columbiana County Recorder in Lisbon, the county seat. The office phone is 330-424-9517, and the recorder's site says documents are recorded and searchable as soon as they are received.

faqs.q: What is the state base fee to record a deed here?
faqs.a: ORC 317.32 sets $17 plus a $17 housing trust fund fee for the first two pages, and $4 plus $4 for each added page. The county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5, so ask the office for its current amount.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Columbiana County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. ORC 319.202 puts the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax on the grantor, while the buyer files the statement of value.

faqs.q: Is a deed between family members free of the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Some are. ORC 319.54 exempts a gift between spouses or between a parent and child, and a transfer among heirs when no money changes hands. The reason for the exemption has to be written on the value statement.

faqs.q: Does a deed count if it is never recorded?
faqs.a: It exists, but ORC 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later buyer who had no knowledge of it. Recording protects the new owner's claim to the house.
